title: Genie_(AI_model)
summary:
Genie is a series of foundation world models developed by Google DeepMind, capable of generating interactive virtual environments from text prompts, images, photographs, or sketches. World models are AI systems that simulate the dynamics of an environment, predicting how they evolve and how actions affect them.

Genie 1 was the first iteration, capable of creating interactive virtual environments from a single image. Genie 2, released later, is a foundation world model capable of generating action-controllable, playable 3D environments for training and evaluating embodied agents. Based on a single prompt image, it can be played by a human or AI agent using keyboard and mouse inputs, generating consistent worlds for up to a minute.

Genie 3 represents a significant advancement. According to Shlomi Fruchter, a research director at DeepMind, Genie 3 is the first real-time interactive general-purpose world model. It can generate photorealistic environments that can be explored in real-time at 20-24 frames per second at 720p resolution for multiple minutes, a significant jump from Genie 2's 10 to 20 seconds. Genie 3 teaches itself how physics works using self-supervised learning rather than using a hard-coded physics engine. Its simulations stay physically consistent over time because the model can remember what it previously generated.

Google has rolled out access to Project Genie for Google AI Ultra subscribers in the US, as an experimental research prototype that lets users create, explore and remix their own interactive worlds. DeepMind views world models as a key stepping stone on the path to AGI, since they make it possible to train AI agents in an unlimited curriculum of rich simulation environments.
